meta.description: The Level-2 mechanical extension. Four alternatives all perform 'transmit torque between shaft and hub', but through different behaviors — and it is the behavior that decides the failure modes and the verification.

meta.title: Mechanical design — Function · Behavior · Structure

data.definition: Two or more load types acting together, e.g. bending with torsion.
data.label: Combined Loading

data.definition: A designed artifact treated as atomic at the level of decomposition currently under consideration. Atomicity is relative to the analysis, not absolute: a rolling bearing is a component to a shaft designer and an assembly to a bearing manufacturer.
data.label: Component

data.definition: Load that varies repeatedly with time, so that fatigue is a candidate failure mechanism.
data.label: Cyclic Loading

data.definition: Any deliberate characteristic of an artifact -- geometric, material, dimensional or procedural -- introduced to influence behaviour, for example to mitigate a failure mode.
data.label: Design Feature

data.definition: Any human-made entity that is the intended outcome of a design process, and about which functions, requirements and design decisions can be asserted. Deliberately domain-neutral: a designed artifact may be mechanical, electrical, software or organisational.
data.label: Designed Artifact
data.scopeNote: Use for the thing being designed, not for the design description of it. A drawing of a shaft is a document, not a DesignedArtifact.

data.definition: A named, bounded portion of an artifact's shape that carries design intent, for example a groove, a fillet, a shoulder or a hole. Geometry features are the usual carriers of stress concentration and of manufacturing and inspection requirements.
data.label: Geometry Feature

data.definition: A region, surface or logical boundary at which two artifacts meet and exchange force, motion, energy, matter or information. Interfaces carry the compatibility conditions that decide whether one design alternative can physically replace another.
data.label: Interface
data.scopeNote: Interface is reified rather than modelled as a bare relation because substitution reasoning must attach conditions, tolerances and required modifications to the junction itself.

data.definition: The motion regime in which the artifact operates.
data.label: Kinematic Condition

data.definition: How force, moment or pressure is applied over time.
data.label: Loading Condition

data.definition: A substance, or a specified condition of a substance, from which an artifact is made, and to which property values such as strength, stiffness and hardness can be attributed.
data.label: Material
data.scopeNote: A Material instance should name its specification and condition together where the source does so (for example 'SAE 1018 low-carbon steel'), because property values are condition-dependent.

data.definition: Motion of one mating part with respect to another across a shared interface, such as axial sliding of a hub along a shaft while torque is transmitted.
data.label: Relative Motion Between Mating Parts
data.scopeNote: A decisive condition for shaft/hub connection choice, and the reason several alternatives that share the function 'transmit torque' are nonetheless not interchangeable.

data.definition: Cyclic loading whose direction reverses, e.g. a shaft driven in both directions.
data.label: Reversing Loading

data.definition: A designed artifact composed of interacting sub-artifacts that together deliver a function no single sub-artifact delivers alone, and whose boundary to its environment is explicitly identified.
data.label: Technical System

data.definition: The mounted element must be re-assembled at a choice of discrete angular positions.
data.label: Angular Indexing

data.definition: Test of the torque a specific assembled connection carries before slipping or yielding.
data.label: Assembly torque test

data.definition: The mounted element must translate along the shaft while torque is being transmitted.
data.label: Axial Sliding Under Torque
data.scopeNote: This condition alone eliminates several otherwise equivalent shaft/hub connection alternatives, and is one of the clearest cases where a shared function does not imply substitutability.

data.definition: The mounted element must be repositionable along the shaft, but only while unloaded.
data.label: Axial Sliding Without Torque

data.definition: Permanent deformation of a mating flank under compressive bearing stress, occurring on whichever of the contacting parts has the lower compressive strength.
data.label: Bearing (compressive crushing) failure

data.definition: Compressive load distributed over a mating flank area, assessed against a compressive strength or an allowable bearing pressure.
data.label: Bearing Pressure Loading

data.definition: The interface between a bearing ring and the shaft or housing that carries it.
data.label: Bearing Seat Interface

data.definition: Operation in which the driven direction reverses, so that a connection with backlash is loaded alternately on opposite flanks.
data.label: Bidirectional Rotation
data.scopeNote: A decisive condition for shaft/hub connections: clearance that is harmless under unidirectional drive becomes impact loading when the direction reverses.

data.definition: Permanent indentation of a raceway by a rolling element under a static load, named for its resemblance to a Brinell hardness impression.
data.label: Brinelling
Circular Cutter Milling
data.scopeNote: Produces a keyseat with a run-out end (a sled-runner keyseat).

data.label: Coefficient of Friction
data.scopeNote: A property of a contacting pair and its surface state, not of one material alone; store it against the interface where the source does so.

data.definition: The characteristic loading of a rotating shaft carrying transverse loads.
data.label: Combined Bending and Torsion

data.definition: Loss of angular or axial registration between mating parts that were intended to move together.
data.label: Connection slip

data.definition: An interface at which bodies transmit load through concentrated or distributed contact while moving relative to one another.
data.label: Rolling or Sliding Contact Interface

data.definition: Load transmitted through a small contact region, producing locally high subsurface stress.
data.label: Contact Loading

data.definition: Fatigue accelerated by a corrosive environment acting at the crack tip.
data.label: Corrosion fatigue

data.definition: Torque is shared among several engaged flanks, reducing the load carried by any one of them relative to a single inserted member.
data.label: Distributed tooth contact
End Milling
data.scopeNote: Produces a keyseat with an abrupt end (a profile keyseat).

data.definition: A stress level below which a material is taken to sustain cyclic loading indefinitely.
data.label: Endurance Limit
data.scopeNote: Both source books distinguish a laboratory-specimen value from an estimated actual value corrected for the part. They use different symbols and partly different correction factors, so the two notions are kept as separate claims joined by an alignment, not merged.

data.definition: Deformation within the elastic range that is nonetheless large enough to prevent a required function.
data.label: Excessive deflection

data.definition: Progressive cracking under repeated stress, typically starting at a surface discontinuity or an internal flaw.
data.label: Fatigue crack initiation and growth

data.definition: The specified dimensional relationship between mating parts, expressed through their tolerance zones.
data.label: Fit

data.definition: Dimensional inspection confirming that mating parts fall within the tolerance zones assumed by the design calculation.
data.label: Fit and tolerance inspection

data.definition: Wear and surface damage caused by small-amplitude oscillatory relative motion between nominally fixed mating surfaces.
data.label: Fretting

data.definition: Loss of the frictional grip on which a connection's torque capacity depends.
data.label: Gross slip at a friction interface

data.definition: Torque is carried by friction generated by a normal pressure at the interface, so capacity depends on the coefficient of friction and on the pressure being maintained in service.
data.label: Frictional load transfer
data.scopeNote: The dependence on a maintained pressure, and on a friction coefficient that is rarely known precisely, is what makes friction-based connections behave differently under shock and thermal cycling from form-locking ones.

data.definition: Operation at a rotational speed high enough that balance, concentricity or critical-speed effects become design drivers.
data.label: Elevated Rotational Speed Condition
data.scopeNote: Deliberately NOT given a numeric boundary. Whether a speed is 'high' depends on the element, its geometry and its supports. Any boundary must be introduced as a mdcore:ThresholdDefinition citing a source and a context.

data.definition: Generating process using a hob cutter, used for gear teeth and for involute splines.
data.label: Hobbing

data.definition: A fit in which the shaft is larger than the hole before assembly, so that assembly generates interface pressure.
data.label: Interference Fit

data.definition: A groove machined in a shaft or a hub bore to receive a key.
data.label: Keyseat
data.scopeNote: Both source books treat the shaft groove and the hub groove as keyseats, with 'keyway' commonly used for the hub groove. The terminology difference is recorded as a ConceptAlignment rather than resolved by fiat.

data.definition: A protective function. Distinguished from TransmitTorque because an element may be required to fail, and a substitution that removes this function is not function-preserving even if torque capacity is unchanged.
data.label: Limit transmitted torque

data.definition: Progressive loss of a preload or clamping force in service.
data.label: Loosening

data.definition: A standardised or generically recognised mechanical component type whose design is treated as a self-contained problem with its own selection procedure, failure modes and verification methods.
data.label: Machine Element
data.scopeNote: Machine-element *families* are defined in the machine-elements module. This class is their common root.

data.definition: A process by which an artifact's geometry, material state or surface is produced or altered.
data.label: Manufacturing Process

data.definition: The processing state in which a material is supplied or used -- cold-drawn, hot-rolled, quenched and tempered, case-hardened -- which conditions its property values.
data.label: Material Condition

data.definition: A named, measurable property of a material in a stated condition.
data.label: Material Property

data.definition: A designed artifact whose required functions are delivered principally through the transmission, transformation, support or containment of mechanical force, motion or energy.
data.label: Mechanical Artifact

data.definition: An interface across which mechanical force, torque or motion is exchanged.
data.label: Mechanical Interface

data.definition: An assembly of mechanical elements arranged to deliver a system-level function such as a power transmission or a motion stage.
data.label: Mechanical System

data.definition: Departure of mating axes from their nominal collinear or parallel relationship.
data.label: Misalignment

data.definition: Deliberately the converse of LocateAxially: an ontology that conflates the two cannot express why a slip-fitted spline and an interference fit are not interchangeable.
data.label: Permit axial motion under torque

data.definition: Permanent local deformation produced when a static contact load exceeds the material's capacity, without relative motion.
data.label: Static plastic indentation

data.definition: Angular lost motion at a connection before load is picked up on the opposite flank.
data.label: Rotational Backlash

data.definition: The interface between a rotating shaft and the bore of a mounted element such as a gear, sheave, sprocket or coupling.
data.label: Shaft/Hub Interface
data.scopeNote: Named explicitly because it is the interface at which several distinct connection alternatives compete, and therefore the one whose compatibility governs their substitutability.

data.definition: Separation across a plane loaded predominantly in shear.
data.label: Shear failure

data.definition: Torque is carried by an inserted member loaded in direct shear over a defined shear area, with a complementary bearing action on its flanks.
data.label: Shear load transfer

data.definition: Comparison of the computed direct shear stress on the governing plane against an allowable shear stress.
data.label: Direct shear stress check

data.definition: Cold working that introduces compressive residual stress at the surface.
data.label: Shot Peening

data.definition: A clearance fit loose enough to permit relative axial motion of the mating parts in service.
data.label: Slip Fit

data.definition: A geometry feature that locally elevates stress above the nominal value, characterised by a stress-concentration factor.
data.label: Stress Raiser

data.definition: The ratio of minimum to maximum stress in a cycle, which characterises a cyclic loading case.
data.label: Stress Ratio Condition
data.scopeNote: Quantified through mdcore:conditionParameter with unit 'dimensionless'.

data.definition: Carry the reaction loads of a rotating shaft while permitting its rotation.
data.label: Support a rotating shaft

data.definition: Subsurface-initiated fatigue under repeated rolling contact stress, appearing as spalling or pitting.
data.label: Surface (contact) fatigue

data.definition: Treatment raising surface hardness to resist wear or to raise fatigue strength.
data.label: Surface Hardening

data.definition: Assembly achieved by heating the outer member or cooling the inner member to create temporary clearance.
data.label: Thermal (Shrink or Chill) Assembly

data.definition: Axial load carried across a rotating interface, e.g. by a bearing.
data.label: Thrust Loading

data.definition: Convey mechanical power from a source to a load.
data.label: Transmit power

data.definition: Convey torque across the interface between a rotating shaft and the bore of an element mounted on it.
data.label: Transmit torque between shaft and hub
data.scopeNote: The pilot function of this ontology version: several distinct machine elements realise it through different behaviors, which makes it the natural setting for demonstrating substitution.

data.definition: Loading whose amplitude changes over the duty cycle, requiring damage accumulation rather than a single-amplitude assessment.
data.label: Variable Loading
Viscous pressure generation in a converging film

data.definition: A machine element whose primary function is to join two members so that load or motion passes between them, while defining their relative position.
data.label: Connection Element
data.scopeNote: The pilot family of this ontology version. Its members compete for a single function -- transmit torque between a shaft and a mounted element -- which makes it the clearest setting for substitution reasoning.

data.definition: A connection element joining two shafts end to end to transmit torque.
data.label: Coupling

data.definition: A machine element that stores mechanical energy and returns it in a controlled way.
data.label: Energy Storage Element

data.definition: A machine element whose primary function is to hold parts together, typically through a preload or a permanent bond, rather than to transmit a working torque.
data.label: Fastening Element
data.scopeNote: Overlaps ConnectionElement by design: a setscrew is both. The families answer different questions and are not partitioned.

data.definition: A toothed element transmitting power between shafts by conjugate tooth action.
data.label: Gear

data.definition: A machine element that starts, stops or modulates the transmission of power or the motion of a member.
data.label: Motion Control Element
data.scopeNote: Added beyond the seven families of the original outline because clutches and brakes are functionally distinct from steady power transmission: their defining function is to interrupt or dissipate, not to convey.

data.definition: A machine element that constrains motion to an intended path.
data.label: Motion Guidance Element

data.definition: Two or more parallel keys sharing the torque, spaced around the shaft.
data.label: Multiple parallel key connection

data.definition: The baseline shaft/hub connection: a separate parallel key in matching shaft and hub keyseats.
data.label: Parallel key connection
data.scopeNote: LimitTransmittedTorque is listed because the key is commonly intended as the sacrificial member; whether that intent applies is a claim, evidenced separately.

data.definition: A machine element whose primary function is to convey mechanical power between locations, optionally changing speed, torque or direction.
data.label: Power Transmission Element

data.definition: A ring seated in a groove to locate a component axially.
data.label: Retaining Ring

data.definition: A machine element that restricts the passage of fluid or contaminant across an interface.
data.label: Sealing Element
